name: Hairline tattoo

lead: A hairline tattoo, formally scalp micropigmentation (SMP), is a superficial cosmetic tattoo that mimics tiny hair follicles. It can recreate a buzz cut on a bald scalp, add apparent density to thinning areas, draw in a hairline, and conceal hair transplant scars.

Pigment is deposited into the epidermis and upper dermis, with ink matched to hair colour. The visible change is immediate. Sourcing on it is mostly industry and press, and no clinical trials were found.

paras: It is typically done over three to four sessions of about two hours, sometimes after a patch test for ink allergy. The hairline is described as the most crucial part, and can be adjusted or touched up relatively easily.

The main risks named are an unnatural result from poor hairline work and possible ink allergies. No scientific data on long-term effects were found. The pigment is described as permanent but removable by laser.

angle.text: Users get scalp micropigmentation to create the look of a closely shaved head or added density along a thinning hairline, and to conceal transplant scars. The change is visible immediately; sources are mostly industry and press, with no clinical trials.

lead: A hairline tattoo, more formally scalp micropigmentation (SMP) or hair tattoo, is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo that creates the look of closely shaved hair on a bald scalp or adds the appearance of density to thinning areas such as the crown and hairline.[1] People use it to get a defined, full-looking hairline and buzz-cut appearance without surgery, and to conceal hair transplant scars and other scars or burn marks on the head.[1]

Unlike a traditional tattoo, SMP is described as superficial, depositing pigment in the epidermis and upper dermis in ink matched to the person's hair colour so that the dots read as tiny hair follicles.[1] The procedure is described as suitable for all ethnicities, and microblading has also been used to address thinning at the hairline.[1]

The hairline is described as one of the most crucial parts of the work, because poor execution there can look unnatural, though a hairline can be adjusted or touched up relatively easily as a person's needs change.[1] No clinical trials of SMP were found; the Wikipedia article draws on news and magazine coverage.

paras: SMP creates the effect of a close buzz cut on a bald head or extra density on a thinning crown by depositing pigment that mimics tiny hair follicles.[1] It is also used to hide the visual impact of hair transplant scars, burns or other scars on the scalp.[1]

Treatment usually takes three to four sessions of about two hours each, with ink colour matched to the person's current hair follicle colour.[1] Practitioners may do a small patch test on an inconspicuous area of the scalp first to check for ink allergies.[1]
Because the hairline is the most crucial element, it can be adjusted or touched up over time as the person's needs change.[1] Cost depends on location, the clinic and the severity of hair loss.[1]
SMP is described as a permanent treatment, and it can be removed with laser treatment.[1]

The main risks mentioned are an unnatural finish from a poorly placed hairline and possible allergy to ink. The Wikipedia article says there are no scientific data on long-term side effects when ink comes from a reputable distributor, a statement it flags as unsourced.[1]
